query_text: Create a web app that takes raw podcast recordings and turns the spoken words into editable text so I can fix the awkward pauses and filler words before posting it anywhere, because right now I am copying and pasting stuff from three different places and it is a total mess, and I want to be able to clean up the transcript and then hit one button to publish it to my podcast feed without touching a single other tool.

Need a web app that shows me in one place how many people are actually opening my newsletter each week, which links they click, whether new readers are signing up or old ones are leaving, and a simple view of whether the paying subscriber count is going up or down, because right now I am hunting through four different spreadsheets to piece together the same basic numbers every Monday morning.

Need a web app for tracking story pitches from writers so the whole editorial team stops losing submissions in email threads, where someone can submit a pitch with a short summary and the editors can leave notes and move it through stages like received, reviewing, approved, or rejected, and everyone on the team sees the same current status without having to ask in a group chat.

Create a web app that shows me which articles on my site have a metered paywall stopping readers and how many of those readers actually end up subscribing, so I can tell whether the wall is set too tight or too loose, because right now I have no idea if readers are bouncing off the paywall angry or if they are converting fine and I am just guessing when I tweak the free article limit.

Need a web app where I can write a short breaking news alert, pick which audience or topic segment gets it, preview exactly how it will look on someone's phone before sending, and then send it in one click, because right now writing a notification means logging into three different systems and I always forget a step and the alert goes out with a typo or to the wrong group.

Create a website for a historical architecture and landmark destination that feels like flipping through a beautifully printed coffee table book in a browser, where each building gets its own full-screen photograph and a little written story beside it, the whole thing moves slowly and deliberately like it respects the age of the places it is showing, and visitors on desktop can browse by era or material so the site itself feels like a piece of considered design rather than a directory.

Create a website for a religious site or place of worship that carries a sense of quietness and reverence the moment someone opens it in their browser, where the photography is generous and unhurried, the written descriptions feel thoughtful rather than rushed, and someone visiting on a desktop computer can navigate by the different areas of the site or the history of the building without the whole thing feeling like a tourist brochure.

A website for a public library's digital collections where the feeling is warm and a little scholarly at the same time, like a reading room you can walk through in your browser, with large previews of manuscripts and photographs and printed materials organized so a visitor on desktop can browse by subject or time period, and the whole site has the kind of quiet confidence that makes you want to linger rather than skim.

A website for a national archive's digital exhibits that feels like stepping into a grand reading room through your desktop browser, where historical documents and photographs are displayed with real breathing room around them and a gentle sense of discovery, so someone browsing can move from one era or collection to the next and feel like they are exploring something curated with genuine care rather than just clicking through a filing system.

Create a website for a performing arts center that shows off both the current season and the rich history of the venue, where the photography feels cinematic and the whole experience in a desktop browser has the atmosphere of a well-designed program booklet, with a way to browse past productions and read about the building itself so that visitors come away feeling like they have discovered something with real cultural weight.

Build a website for a city symphony orchestra that feels serious and beautiful at the same time when opened in a desktop browser, where upcoming concerts and the orchestra's history are presented with the same care you would expect from a printed season brochure, the typography feels chosen rather than defaulted, and someone visiting can move from current performances to the ensemble's story and background without the site ever feeling rushed or cluttered.

Create a website for a national park visitor information and heritage site that has the unhurried, wide-open feeling of the landscape itself when someone opens it in a desktop browser, where full-width landscape photographs do most of the storytelling and the written information about trails and history and ecology sits beside the imagery without competing with it, and the overall tone feels like a beautifully made guidebook rather than a government form.

Build a website for documenting indigenous peoples' cultural heritage that carries genuine visual weight and respect, where the photography and oral histories and material culture are presented in a desktop browser with real care for how things are laid out and the pace at which a visitor encounters them, the color and texture of the design feel drawn from the culture being documented rather than from a generic template, and browsing it feels like an act of attention rather than a quick scroll.

A website for a UNESCO world heritage site's official portal that opens in a desktop browser and immediately communicates grandeur through generous photography and unhurried pacing, where each section of the site feels like a chapter in a well-edited book about the place, visitors can explore the significance, the history, and the current conservation efforts without the page ever feeling crowded, and the whole visual language says this place has been here for centuries and the site was designed to match.

Build a website for a literary foundation and writers house that has the feel of a beloved independent bookshop translated into a browser experience, where the typography is warm and the photography of the building and the writers who passed through it is generous and unhurried, someone on a desktop can browse the foundation's history and current residency programs and reading events, and the whole site has a personality that feels shaped by people who care about literature rather than people who care about website metrics.

Make a website for a national film archive and cinematheque that has the moody, considered feeling of a retrospective program booklet opened in a desktop browser, where film stills and poster art are given real space to breathe and the history of the collection is told with the kind of editorial voice you expect from a serious arts institution, and visitors can browse by director or decade or genre and feel like they are moving through a place that genuinely loves cinema.

Build a website for a natural history museum's specimen and diorama gallery that captures the feeling of wandering through a grand Victorian hall when someone opens it in their desktop browser, where the photography of taxidermy, fossils, and recreated scenes is dramatic and lit beautifully, the written descriptions feel like they were written by someone who has memorized every label, and browsing by geological era or animal family feels like flipping through a gorgeous illustrated encyclopedia.

Create a website for a botanic garden's plant collections and ecology programs that feels lush and carefully observed when opened in a desktop browser, where close-up botanical photography and seasonal imagery set the tone and the written content about individual plant families and the garden's conservation work sits alongside the visuals in a way that feels like a beautifully produced nature journal, and visitors can browse by collection or habitat and the whole experience rewards slow looking.

A web app for publishing an advocacy manifesto or open letter where the visual presentation in a desktop browser feels as deliberate and charged as the words themselves, with bold typographic choices and a layout that draws the eye through each section of the argument in a clear sequence, so someone reading it feels the weight of the statement rather than just scanning a wall of text, and the design makes the cause feel serious and worth the reader's full attention.

Create a web app for publishing official announcements and public notices that feels clear and dignified in a desktop browser rather than cluttered and bureaucratic, where each announcement is presented with enough breathing room that readers can actually find what they need, the visual hierarchy guides the eye from the most urgent information down to the supporting details, and the overall feeling is that the organization behind it takes communication seriously and respects the reader's time.

A web app for a city's open data portal where residents can actually find and understand the public information their city collects, designed so that browsing it on a desktop browser feels like exploring something made for curious people rather than data professionals, with clean visual groupings by topic and a presentation style that makes charts and tables feel inviting rather than intimidating, and the whole experience communicates that the data belongs to the people looking at it.

Need a website for a digital oral history collection where recorded voices and their transcripts are presented together in a desktop browser with the kind of care and warmth the stories deserve, where portraits of the speakers are given real space and the written text alongside the audio feels edited and considered rather than raw, and someone browsing the collection can move between stories by theme or place and feel like they are encountering real lives rather than files in a database.

Create a website for a nonprofit's annual impact report that tells the year's story in a way that actually holds someone's attention in a desktop browser rather than reading like a spreadsheet with a logo on it, where data and personal stories are woven together with photography and the visual pacing gives each section room to land, and the overall feeling is that real work happened and real people were affected and the organization wants you to understand both.

A website for documenting a cultural heritage site virtually where opening it in a desktop browser feels like arriving at the place itself, with photography and video that gives the location genuine presence, the historical and architectural context written in a voice that is knowledgeable without being dry, and a way to move through the site section by section that mirrors the experience of actually walking through the space so visitors come away feeling like they have been somewhere rather than read something.

Need a website for an environmental NGO's field research findings where the photography from the field does real storytelling work in a desktop browser and the data and written summaries are presented with enough visual clarity that someone who is not a scientist can follow the thread of the research, the layout has the serious but human feeling of a well-produced long-form magazine piece, and browsing through different study regions or species feels like moving through something that genuinely cares about what it is reporting.

Need a web app for an indigenous language preservation and learning resource site that feels as beautiful and reverent as the culture it represents, with warm earthy tones, hand-drawn-style illustrations woven into the layout, and a browsing experience on desktop that lets you move through audio recordings, story texts, and vocabulary guides the way you'd slowly leaf through a treasured book.

Build a browser-based catalogue tool for a museum's permanent collection where each artwork gets generous breathing room on screen, a muted gallery-white background, and the kind of quiet typography you'd find in a high-end art book, with a left-side filter panel for medium and era that feels curated rather than cluttered, so browsing feels genuinely pleasurable.

A human rights case documentation and reporting tool for desktop browsers where the visual tone is serious and trustworthy, think deep navy and clean serif type, with a left-hand navigation that lets you browse cases by country or category, and each case entry lays out the facts in a clear, editorial style that feels credible and respectful to the people involved.

Build a web app for browsing government audit and transparency reports that looks like it was designed with actual care, where the layout feels clean and legible rather than like a government PDF dumped online, with a well-organized sidebar for filtering by agency or year and individual report entries that display key findings in a way that feels scannable and trustworthy for desktop use.

Create a website for a literary foundation's author essay and spotlight hub that has the quiet, considered feel of a good literary magazine, with generous margins, beautiful type choices, and a browsing layout for desktop where you can explore authors and their essays side by side, the kind of reading environment that makes you want to slow down and stay awhile.

Make a web app for publishing archaeological excavation findings that has the mood of an explorer's field journal brought to the browser, with aged-parchment tones, well-composed photo spreads, and a desktop layout where site overviews sit alongside artifact close-ups and written findings, giving the whole thing a sense of discovery and visual coherence that honors the work.

Build a volunteer recruitment web app that feels like it was made by people who actually care, not some corporate HR portal, where the personality comes through in the tone and layout, you can browse open opportunities on desktop with a warm but confident look, and signing up to help feels like joining something meaningful rather than filling out a form.

A donation campaign web app for desktop that carries real weight and intention, where the cause is front and center with a look that says this matters, a fundraising goal tracker that feels honest rather than gimmicky, and a giving flow that respects the donor's attention, the kind of site that makes you feel good about where your money is going.

Need a website for a museum membership annual drive that has a real identity, something that feels warm and cultured rather than like a generic charity ask, with the membership tiers laid out clearly on desktop so visitors can actually compare what they get, and the whole thing carrying the same tasteful energy as the museum itself.

A symphony orchestra season ticket promotional site for desktop that actually sounds like it belongs to a world-class ensemble, with rich dark tones and elegant type that set the mood before a note is played, a season program laid out so you can see the full lineup at a glance, and a ticket selection flow that feels as polished as the hall itself.

A centennial anniversary celebration site for a national park, built as a web app for desktop, that carries the identity of something genuinely worth honoring, with sweeping landscape photography given full room to breathe, a timeline of the park's hundred-year history laid out with care, and a tone that feels proud and alive rather than institutional and stiff.

Create a web app for a city tourism official destination campaign that actually has a point of view, something that makes the city feel alive and worth visiting rather than a brochure, with bold photography leading the layout on desktop, neighborhoods and highlights browsable in a way that feels like insider knowledge, and a voice that gives the city real personality.

Need a web app for a theater company that showcases their current and upcoming productions with genuine theatrical energy, where the site on desktop feels like stepping into the lobby, productions get their own spotlight with cast info and atmosphere photos, and buying a ticket feels like a natural next step rather than an afterthought buried in a corner.

Create a web app for a cultural festival that actually earns the excitement of the event, built for desktop browsers with a bold and festive look, a schedule of performances and activities laid out in a way that is easy to scan and save, and a ticket-buying flow that moves quickly so people can grab passes before they sell out.

Build a film festival web app where audiences can vote for their favorite films for the audience award and sponsors get a dignified showcase that feels like part of the festival rather than an interruption, the whole thing working in desktop browsers with a cinematic look, dark palette, and a voting section that feels participatory and fun rather than bureaucratic.

Make a web app for a heritage preservation monument sponsorship site that actually makes donors feel like patrons of something lasting and beautiful, with the monument's history told through gorgeous imagery on desktop, sponsorship tiers presented with a sense of dignity rather than price tags, and a look that feels as enduring as the stone it is trying to protect.

Create a fundraising and impact site for a public library capital campaign, built as a web app for desktop, where the whole thing feels like it belongs to a place that believes in community and knowledge, with a giving progress tracker that looks hopeful rather than desperate, donor spotlights that feel personal, and a tone that makes supporting the library feel genuinely good.

Need a web app for an environmental pledge campaign that actually has the soul and urgency the cause deserves, running in a desktop browser with a look that is striking and committed, where visitors can browse the coalition partners with pride, sign their pledge in a moment that feels meaningful, and see the growing wall of names as something genuinely moving.

A food bank hunger awareness month donation site for desktop browsers that carries real heart and directness, where the impact numbers are given the weight they deserve, the donation flow is clean and quick so nothing gets in the way of giving, and the whole site has a warm, grounded identity that makes you feel connected to the people being helped.

Make a donation web app that just works without making people jump through hoops, a browser-based tool where someone can pick an amount, choose a cause or project to support, and complete the whole thing in a few clicks on desktop without having to create an account first or sit through five confirmation screens before their money actually goes anywhere.

Need a membership renewal web app that stops making it so painful to pay for another year, a website where I can log in on my desktop, see exactly when my membership expires, pick a renewal plan, and pay without having to dig through emails or call anyone, the whole renewal handled in one place with a receipt I can actually find later.

Need a web app for buying licensed art prints and reproductions from a museum collection, where I can browse the available works on desktop, see exactly what sizes and formats are available for each piece, and complete the licensing or purchase without having to email someone back and forth or figure out a separate form buried in the museum's main site.

Create a booking and payment web app for guided tours at heritage sites where you can see available tour times right away on desktop, pick a date, choose how many people, and pay all in one place without being bounced between different systems, plus get a simple confirmation with the tour details so you actually know what you signed up for.

Build a venue rental reservation web app for a cultural center that lets people check room availability on a desktop browser, see what each space includes and how much it costs per hour, submit a booking request with their event details, and get a confirmation without having to track down a coordinator by phone just to find out if a room is open.

Need a performing arts season ticket purchase website that makes it easy to see the full season schedule on desktop, compare what each ticket package covers, pick your seats or package tier, and pay without having to wade through a clunky old ticketing system that times out every five minutes and loses your cart.
